error_chain: Spring's TransactionTemplate wraps the operation in a JTA-style transaction via JpaTransactionManager which delegates flush decisions to the EntityManager
Hibernate's SessionImpl owns the dirty-entity action queue; an HQL query triggers DefaultAutoFlushEventListener which flushes pending actions before the query runs
A native SQL query path bypasses DefaultAutoFlushEventListener because Hibernate cannot determine which entities the SQL touches; FlushMode.AUTO does not apply to native queries

The native query reads the database directly, sees the pre-save value, and Hibernate's first-level cache still holds the new value; the transaction commits with the discrepancy invisible until downstream code re-reads
trigger_conditions: Customer's @Transactional method calls save() then immediately executes a native query (entityManager.createNativeQuery)
Hibernate's auto-flush listener does not fire for native queries, so dirty entities are not written before the SQL executes
Spring's JpaTransactionManager defers the flush to commit, leaving the in-method native read against stale persistent state

expected_answer.error_origin: Hibernate's DefaultAutoFlushEventListener not firing for native SQL paths in SessionImpl
expected_answer.bypass_reason: Spring's JpaTransactionManager only flushes at commit; it does not insert a flush before a native query because Hibernate's auto-flush is the contract
expected_answer.correct_config: Either explicitly call entityManager.flush() before the native query, or set FlushMode.ALWAYS on the query, or restructure to use HQL/Criteria so Hibernate's auto-flush fires
